name: Coheed and Cambria
label: Equal Vision
lede: A Nyack, New York band that fell apart over gas money, came back as a science-fiction saga, went gold on a hardcore label, and has spent thirty years telling one story across ten of its eleven albums while its rhythm section fought addiction, rehab and a pharmacy robbery.

eras.title: Gas money and a naked prey
eras.text: In Nyack, New York, Claudio Sanchez and Travis Stever went through band names like guitar strings. What stuck was Shabütie, a funk-punk-metal grab bag that slowly turned into the vehicle for a science-fiction story Sanchez was writing.

years.h: Beautiful Loser breaks up over gas money
years.p: After Toxic Parents, Claudio Sanchez and Travis Stever form Beautiful Loser with drummer Nate Kelley and bassist Jon Carleo. By June 1995 an argument over gas money ends it, and Stever walks.

years.h: The trio renames itself Shabütie
years.p: Sanchez, Kelley and Carleo take the name Shabütie from a chant in the 1965 film The Naked Prey, and play everything from punk to funk to heavy metal.

years.h: Guitarist [[Michael Todd|e0add4a2-5a48-4ed6-a52e-721074716c3f]] switches to bass
years.p: Jon Carleo leaves Shabütie and Michael Todd, mainly a guitarist, is recruited to play bass.

years.h: Travis Stever returns on the Penelope EP
years.p: Shabütie releases the demo Plan to Take Over the World and The Penelope EP, and Travis Stever rejoins.

years.h: Nate Kelley quits in the middle of a show
years.p: Drummer Nate Kelley leaves during a live performance. His replacement is Josh Eppard, drummer in his brother Joey Eppard's band 3.

years.h: The Delirium Trigger EP, and a new name
years.p: The band renames itself Coheed and Cambria after the husband-and-wife heroes of Claudio Sanchez's sci-fi story, with the Keywork as its logo. On Delirium Trigger, Kelley drums but Eppard gets the credit.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the decision to rename to a 1998 trip to Paris. Several Delirium Trigger songs became the comic The Bag.On.Line Adventures, later retitled The Amory Wars. The Keywork is the alignment of 78 worlds in that story.

years.h: Recording the debut in Paramus, New Jersey
years.p: Coheed and Cambria record The Second Stage Turbine Blade at Stainglass Studio in Paramus with Michael Birnbaum and Chris Bittner, the producers they'll use for years.

eras.title: Gold on a hardcore label
eras.text: Equal Vision Records, Steve Reddy's label of Converge, Saves the Day and Krishna hardcore, put out the first two chapters of the saga. The second went gold, and MTV played a band that sang about a sci-fi war as if it were a breakup record.

years.h: The Second Stage Turbine Blade on Equal Vision Records
years.p: Part one of the Amory Wars. [[Dr. Know|0fa99d3d-171f-462c-9620-31e41c2d9b85]] of [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] plays guitar on Time Consumer, and old versions of Delirium Trigger and 33 still feature Nate Kelley.
years.xp: The album has a hidden track, IRO-Bot, tucked into the last song. Devil in Jersey City became the first single and video. Evil Ink put out a ten-issue comic adaptation in 2004, written by Sanchez and drawn by Wes Abbott.

years.h: Japan, and a short stint on Warped Tour
years.p: Coheed and Cambria tours the U.S. and Japan and does a brief run on the 2002 Vans Warped Tour. In August they sign with manager Blaze James.

years.h: In Keeping Secrets of Silent Earth: 3 goes gold
years.p: Recorded at Applehead in Woodstock, New York. It reaches No. 52 on the Billboard 200, No. 5 on the independent chart, and is certified gold by the RIAA.
years.xp: The album runs 69 minutes and ends with a hidden track, 21:13, after a run of silent tracks. Entertainment Weekly named it one of the key albums of the new prog; Robert Christgau called it a dud.
play: In Keeping Secrets of Silent Earth: 3

years.h: A Favor House Atlantic hits MTV
years.p: The single, and later Blood Red Summer in November, put Coheed and Cambria on MTV. They tour with [[Thursday|0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274]], [[Thrice|244afcb7-fa9a-49b1-9aa6-0149512d1c52]], [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]] and [[Rainer Maria|597dd959-1a24-457e-bea0-36f3fee2a5cb]] and win two mtvU Woodies.

years.h: Filming Live at the Starland Ballroom
years.p: Coheed and Cambria films a show at New Jersey's Starland Ballroom. It becomes the band's first live DVD in March 2005.

eras.title: Columbia, rehab and a borrowed drummer
eras.text: Columbia signed the band and Good Apollo went top ten. Then the pressure cracked the rhythm section: Michael Todd went to rehab, Josh Eppard left before he could be fired, and the next album's drums were played by a Foo Fighter.

years.h: Good Apollo, Volume One: No. 7 on Columbia
years.p: Coheed and Cambria's first major-label album, after a multi-album Columbia deal. It sells nearly a million copies, and Welcome Home rides a riff that critics heard as Led Zeppelin's Kashmir.
years.xp: The record pushed the band from melodic post-hardcore toward full progressive rock. Tours with [[The Blood Brothers|b847568f-cd75-44c7-b87b-4f38a5a9f661]], [[Circa Survive|a2496a3c-8f42-4b98-b780-6f8d64f56441]], Dredg, Head Automatica and [[Avenged Sevenfold|24e1b53c-3085-4581-8472-0b0088d2508c]] followed, and Metal Hammer named it album of the year at its 2006 Golden Gods.
play: Good Apollo, I'm Burning Star IV, Volume One: From Fear Through the Eyes of Madness

years.h: Michael Todd leaves a European tour for rehab
years.p: At the start of Coheed and Cambria's 2006 European tour, bassist Michael Todd leaves with a growing heroin addiction and checks into rehab, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Claudio Sanchez's side project, The Prize Fighter Inferno
years.p: Sanchez releases My Brother's Blood Machine, an acoustic-electronic prequel to the Coheed story. He said Coheed itself was first imagined as that kind of side project.

years.big: The drummer left before he could be fired
years.h: Josh Eppard and Michael Todd are out
years.p: Coheed and Cambria announces drummer Josh Eppard's indefinite departure, with bassist Michael Todd also gone. Eppard's struggle with substance abuse, worsened by nonstop touring, was the real reason.
years.xp:
Talk at the time was of creative limits. Eppard later said he was about to be fired anyway. Matt Williams and drum tech Michael Petrak filled in on stage.

Eppard turned the experience into rap records as Weerd Science; his 2011 album Sick Kids is about his addiction.

years.h: Michael Todd returns for No World for Tomorrow
years.p: Todd is back as Coheed and Cambria enter a Los Angeles studio with producer Nick Raskulinecz.

years.h: Chris Pennie joins, but Taylor Hawkins plays the album
years.p: Chris Pennie leaves [[The Dillinger Escape Plan|1bc41dff-5397-4c53-bb50-469d2c277197]] for Coheed and Cambria, but a contract keeps him off the record. [[Taylor Hawkins|f0d35e7c-bbda-4063-a07b-0aa044fa5c8a]] of [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]] plays the drums, working from Pennie's ideas.

years.h: No World for Tomorrow: No. 6 on Columbia
years.p: The fourth album closes the original Amory Wars tetralogy. Coheed and Cambria headline part of Warped Tour and open a 25-city U.S. tour for [[Linkin Park|f59c5520-5f46-4d2c-b2c4-822eabf53419]].
years.xp: The Linkin Park tour forced the band to cancel its Soundwave Festival dates in Australia. The Feathers video, starring Rena Riffel, won Best Music Video at the 2008 Kerrang! Awards, and Welcome Home went into Rock Band that November.
play: Good Apollo, I'm Burning Star IV, Volume Two: No World for Tomorrow

eras.title: Four nights, four albums, then Attleboro
eras.text: The band played its whole catalog one album a night, wrote a prequel with a novel attached, and toured with Slipknot and Heaven & Hell. Then its bassist was arrested at a gig for robbing a pharmacy, and its drummer situation turned over again.

years.h: Neverender: four albums on four nights
years.p: In New York, Chicago, Los Angeles and London, Coheed and Cambria plays one album per night. The CD/DVD box set Neverender: Children of the Fence Edition follows in March 2009.

years.h: On tour with Slipknot, then Heaven & Hell
years.p: Coheed and Cambria opens for [[Slipknot|a466c2a2-6517-42fb-a160-1087c3bafd9f]] and Trivium early in the year and for Heaven & Hell in August, and plays Wacken, Sonisphere and Lollapalooza.

years.h: Year of the Black Rainbow, a prequel with a novel
years.p: The fifth album jumps back before the first one in the Amory Wars story. The deluxe edition comes with a novel by Claudio Sanchez and Peter David.

years.h: Michael Todd arrested at a Coheed show for pharmacy robbery
years.p: Bassist Michael Todd is arrested at the Comcast Center in Mansfield, Massachusetts, on the Soundgarden tour, charged with armed robbery of a Walgreens pharmacy in Attleboro and possessing narcotics.
years.xp: Wes Styles filled in for the rest of the tour, and on August 4 the band announced a mutual decision to part ways. In June 2012 Todd pleaded guilty and was sentenced to a year of home confinement and three years' probation.

years.h: Chris Pennie out, Josh Eppard back
years.p: Chris Pennie leaves by mutual agreement over creative differences, and two weeks later Josh Eppard, gone since 2006, rejoins on drums.

eras.title: The Afterman, and a year off from the saga
eras.text: With Zach Cooper on bass and Eppard back, the lineup finally held. The band split one story across two albums, got a Hollywood film deal that never happened, then stepped outside the Amory Wars for the first time.

years.h: Zach Cooper gets a cold call and the bass job
years.p: Manager Blaze James cold-calls Zach Cooper of AM to AM on a personal recommendation. Cooper is still in the band today.

years.h: Mark Wahlberg signs on to film the Amory Wars
years.p: At San Diego Comic-Con, producers Mark Wahlberg and Stephen Levinson announce a live-action Amory Wars film. Claudio Sanchez said in 2019 that Wahlberg's option had expired.

years.h: The Afterman: Ascension, part one of a double album
years.p: Recorded at Applehead in Woodstock. The story follows Sirius Amory, who discovers the Keywork's energy is an afterlife for departed souls.

years.h: The Afterman: Descension completes the pair
years.p: The second half of the double album comes out four months after the first, with videos for Dark Side of Me and Number City.

years.h: In Keeping Secrets remastered and played in full
years.p: Coheed and Cambria reissues its gold second album and tours with Thank You Scientist, playing it start to finish.

years.h: The Color Before the Sun: the first non-Amory Wars album
years.p: Claudio Sanchez writes about his own life instead: moving from the country to the city and the birth of his son Atlas in June 2014.

years.h: On tour with [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]]
years.p: Coheed and Cambria takes Glassjaw, I the Mighty and Silver Snakes on its U.S. tour, and later tours with [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]] and Polyphia.

eras.title: Vaxis
eras.text: A deal with Roadrunner Records brought the band back to the saga with a new five-part arc, Vaxis, and back to arenas with Mastodon. Three acts in, the story is still unfolding.

years.h: Coheed and Cambria signs with Roadrunner Records
years.p: The band that started on Equal Vision and broke through on Columbia moves to Roadrunner, and teases a return to the Amory Wars.

years.h: Vaxis – Act I: The Unheavenly Creatures
years.p: Coheed and Cambria's ninth album starts a new arc of the Amory Wars.
play: Vaxis – Act I: The Unheavenly Creatures

years.h: The Unheavenly Skye Tour with [[Mastodon|bc5e2ad6-0a4a-4d90-b911-e9a7e6861727]]
years.p: Coheed and Cambria co-headlines with Mastodon, with [[Every Time I Die|ef90f210-f136-4386-ab37-8c00d04eeace]] opening.

years.h: Jessie's Girl 2, with Rick Springfield singing
years.p: Coheed and Cambria writes a sequel to Rick Springfield's 1981 hit, with Springfield on it. Entertainment Weekly reported they'd considered an entire album of sequels to other people's songs.

years.h: Vaxis – Act II: A Window of the Waking Mind
years.p: The tenth album. Claudio Sanchez said some plot points felt insensitive after COVID-19 and needed rethinking. [[Alkaline Trio|69421e11-e4c3-4854-951b-ceab4972e38e]] replaced Dance Gavin Dance on the summer tour.
play: Vaxis – Act II: A Window of the Waking Mind

years.h: Vaxis – Act III: The Father of Make Believe
years.p: Album eleven arrives with the Infinite Arc Tour alongside Mastodon and Periphery, and a deluxe New Entities Edition with four new tracks in October.
